claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_satyavati
claims.summary: Satyavatī is installed in Śāṃtanu’s household as his wife.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: The verse follows their marriage and identifies her as the woman Śāṃtanu has married.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_chitrangada
claims.summary: Citrāṅgada is born to Śāṃtanu and Satyavatī.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_chitrangada
claims.summary: Citrāṅgada is born to Śāṃtanu and Satyavatī.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_vichitravirya
claims.summary: Vicitravīrya is born to Śāṃtanu and Satyavatī.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_vichitravirya
claims.summary: Vicitravīrya is born to Śāṃtanu and Satyavatī.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_bhishma
claims.summary: Satyavatī identifies Bhīṣma as Śāṃtanu’s son and heir to the family’s memorial line.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: Bhīṣma’s mother is not asserted here.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_bhishma
claims.summary: Bhīṣma is referred to as Gāṅgeya, the son of Gaṅgā.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: Gaṅgā is not otherwise included as a node in this batch.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_ambika
claims.summary: Ambikā is given in marriage to Vicitravīrya.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_ambalika
claims.summary: Ambālikā is given in marriage to Vicitravīrya.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_amba
claims.summary: Ambā says she had chosen Śālva as her husband before the svayaṃvara.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_vyasa
claims.summary: Satyavatī recounts that Parāśara fathered her son Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, later called Vyāsa.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_vyasa
claims.summary: Satyavatī calls Dvaipāyana her son, born to her before her marriage to Śāṃtanu.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_vyasa
claims.summary: Satyavatī calls Vyāsa her first son and Vicitravīrya her younger son, and says Vyāsa is Vicitravīrya’s brother through her.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_dhritarashtra
claims.summary: Vyāsa begets Dhṛtarāṣṭra with Vicitravīrya’s widow Ambikā under Satyavatī’s niyoga.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: This is the text’s niyoga conception, distinct from the dynastic/legal fatherhood of Vicitravīrya’s field.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_dhritarashtra
claims.summary: Ambikā is Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s mother in the niyoga account.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_dhritarashtra
claims.summary: Vyāsa is asked to beget heirs in Vicitravīrya’s field; Dhṛtarāṣṭra is born from that arrangement.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: Records the text’s dynastic field relationship, not biological paternity.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu
claims.summary: Vyāsa begets Pāṇḍu with Vicitravīrya’s widow Ambālikā under Satyavatī’s niyoga.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: Distinguish biological begetting from dynastic/legal fatherhood in Vicitravīrya’s field.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu
claims.summary: Ambālikā is Pāṇḍu’s mother in the niyoga account.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu
claims.summary: Pāṇḍu is born through the niyoga for heirs in Vicitravīrya’s dynastic field.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: Not an assertion of biological paternity.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_vidura
claims.summary: Vyāsa begets Vidura with the widows’ unnamed attendant under Satyavatī’s niyoga.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_vidura
claims.summary: The narrative identifies Vidura as Dharma reborn after Māṇḍavya’s curse.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: A rebirth identity claim, not biological parentage.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_mandavya
claims.summary: Māṇḍavya curses Dharma to be born among humans as a śūdra after the unjust punishment.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu
claims.summary: Pāṇḍu marries Kuntī.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_pandu
claims.summary: Pāṇḍu marries Mādrī.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_karna
claims.summary: Kuntī bears Karṇa after invoking the Sun with Durvāsas’s mantra.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: Karṇa’s divine begetting is narrated separately; no human father is inferred.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_karna
claims.summary: Karṇa is conceived through Kuntī’s invocation of the Sun.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator
claims.note: Add the deity node under the name used by the CE.

claims.subject: mb_adi_royal_dhritarashtra
claims.summary: Gāndhārī is identified as Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s wife.
claims.speaker: Vaiśaṃpāyana / narrator

search_log.query: BORI Mahābhārata Critical Edition Ādiparvan 1.95–1.108 Kuru succession and Dhṛtarāṣṭra children
search_log.outcome: Read the BORI CE Unicode Roman e-text at verses 1.95–1.108, checking name spellings, birth-order entries, and direct kinship or niyoga statements. Disambiguated same-spelling roster entries by their distinct positions because the CE itself says the list is in birth order.

notes: Batch is limited to BORI CE Ādiparvan 1.95–1.108 and is separate from other MB batches.

The CE states that Dhṛtarāṣṭra has 101 sons and one daughter (1.107.1, 34–37; 1.108.14). The roster contains 104 grammatical person slots when all dual and triple forms are expanded; three exact names recur (Jalasaṃdha, Sama, Mahābāhu). The batch records 101 person nodes by preserving the roster’s stated total and retains the three repeat positions as unresolved references, since each might name the same son again or a distinct homonymous son. Dual forms (Vindānuvinda, Citropacitra, Nandopananda, Ugrayāyin) and the triple Dṛḍharatha are split according to Sanskrit number; transliterated solo forms are editorial segmentation.

The first three royal princes produced through Vyāsa’s niyoga are represented as biologically begotten by Vyāsa and born to their respective mothers, while Vicitravīrya is recorded only as dynastic field/lineage reference. No biological fatherhood is inferred for Vicitravīrya.
Yuyutsu’s mother and the widows’ attendant remain unnamed; no personal name is fabricated. Karṇa is a child of Kuntī and Sūrya in the invoked-deity episode.
